title: De Finetti Structures in Networks of Quantum Systems
abstract: Consider $N$ identical quantum systems at the vertices of a graph, interacting via pairwise edge couplings. We designate $K$ vertices as a system of interest $\mathrm S$ and the remaining $N-K$ as a reservoir $\mathrm R$. Under generic connectivity assumptions between $\mathrm S$ and $\mathrm R$, we show that for $N\to\infty$, the reduced state of $\mathrm S$ converges to a convex combination of symmetric product states of $K$ single-vertex density matrices -- called a de Finetti representation. Unlike in standard derivations for symmetric (exchangeable) systems, we establish de Finetti representations for quantum networks, which are inherently non-exchangeable. We construct the representations explicitly and quantify the convergence rate. We show that Erdős--Rényi random graphs exhibit the de Finetti structure: as the reservoir grows, the reduced state of any fixed finite subgraph converges almost surely to an explicit deterministic product state. As applications, we establish a general area law for the entanglement entropy of $\mathrm S$, analyze mean-field and fluctuation scalings of the $\mathrm S$-$\mathrm R$ interaction, and illustrate our results on qubit networks. We also derive quantitative convergence estimates for information-theoretic quantities, including von Neumann entropy, mutual information, and entanglement within $\mathrm S$ and between $\mathrm S$ and $\mathrm R$.
summary: This work extends the de Finetti theorem to quantum networks, showing that the reduced state of a subsystem converges to a specific convex combination structure even when the system interactions are non-exchangeable. By analyzing entanglement entropy and information measures, the authors provide quantitative convergence rates for these quantities in the thermodynamic limit. This is crucial for understanding correlations in large, complex quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper determines the structure of the reduced state of a finite subsystem embedded in a large quantum network as the total system size approaches infinity.
main_result: The reduced state converges to a de Finetti representation, extending this structure to quantum networks that are inherently non-exchangeable.
method: The analysis involves taking the partial trace over the reservoir and analyzing the convergence of quantum information measures using various inequalities and scaling limits.
model_or_system: The model consists of N identical quantum systems at graph vertices interacting via pairwise edge couplings, with a subsystem S (size K) coupled to a reservoir R (size N-K).
key_observables: Reduced state ($ho^{(K)}_N$), entanglement entropy, von Neumann entropy, mutual information, and concurrence.
important_parameters: The system size limit ($N 	o \infty$), the connectivity structure (e.g., Erdős–Rényi random graphs), and the scaling of the S-R interaction (mean-field vs. fluctuation).
main_assumptions: Generic connectivity assumptions between S and R, and the system being in a 'well-connected' regime for convergence to hold.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the network structure (S coupled to R). Figure 2 illustrates the concept of effective connectivity ($\epsilon_K(N)$) using incidence numbers to define 'well-connectedness'.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the convergence to the de Finetti structure for non-exchangeable quantum networks. It then analyzes the convergence of specific information-theoretic quantities (entropy, mutual information) in the large N limit, providing explicit convergence rates and bounds.
why_interesting: The generalization of the de Finetti theorem to non-exchangeable quantum networks provides powerful tools for understanding entanglement and correlations in complex, realistic quantum systems beyond simple mean-field approximations.

figures.caption: Figure 1. A network of quantum systems. Each of the N vertices of a graph hosts an identical quantum system (white discs). Every edge in the graph represents the interaction between the quantum systems located at the corresponding vertices. The interaction between vertices i, j is of the form AiAj, where Ai is the single-vertex operator A translated to act on the vertex i. K among the N vertices are singled out to form an open system S which is connected to a reservoir RN consisting of the remaining N −K vertices. As the graph size N is increased, existing edges remain unchanged, while new ones may be added. We analyze the state of the fixed system S as N →∞.

Figure 2. Effective connectivity along a graph sequence. S consisting of K = 3 vertices connected to an R of a growing number N −K = 2, 4, 6 of vertices. L, (2.19) consists of two elements B1, B2 (each one of them is one of the Ai). The system is fixed while reservoir incidence classes accumulate. As the graph grows, the incidence numbers ν1, ν2 associated to B1, B2, (3.2) are growing in the first row, while one of them remains bounded (equal to one) in the bottom row. Accordingly, the effective connection number εK(N), (3.3) grows in N or stays bounded. Growing εK(N) →∞gives a well-connected system S.

Figure 3. Different resolutions of the system by the reservoir. Collective resolution: each vertex in R connected to S is linked to every vertex in S; the set of boundary operators L, (2.19) is a singleton; the CPTP map P, (3.12) is an integral over a ζ-dimensional torus with factorized, symmetric integrand. Coarse resolution: S is subdivided into several subsystems (two in the example depicted); each vertex in R which connects to S is linked to all the vertices of exactly one subsystem; each subsystem contributes to L with one operator; P is the product of actions of the collective type on each subsystem. Figure 4. Area Law in quantum networks. The boundary ∂S of S, (2.15) is induced by the graph: it is the collection of vertices in S which are connected to R. Two representations in which the network is viewed as being 2- and 3-dimensional. The von Neumann entropy of the state of S is called the entanglement entropy when the total network state is pure. The entanglement entropy may grow with S. We show that as N →∞, the system entanglement entropy is bounded above by |∂S|, the area of the boundary of S (not its volume).
